comparisons.peer_topic: New Market Competition and Investment Returns
comparisons.peer_summary: New businesses in AI, cloud-to-edge, and other areas introduce new competition and require significant investment with no guarantee of adequate returns. Failures in AI products or the foundry business could lead to asset impairments, restructuring charges, and opportunity costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclose that significant investments in new and developing technologies carry a risk of not realizing an adequate return. AVGO states generally that 'slow or unsuccessful return of our investments in research and development could adversely affect us.' INTC provides more specific context, noting that 'developing products and market segments require significant investment, do not always grow as projected... and we may not realize an adequate return on our investments,' with specific examples in AI and foundry services.

sentences.text: • We make investments in research and development and the slow or unsuccessful return of our investments in research and development could adversely affect us.

These developing products and market segments require significant investment, do not always grow as projected or at all, or sometimes adopt competing technologies, and we may not realize an adequate return on our investments.

comparisons.peer_summary: Innovation efforts involve significant expense with no guarantee of expected benefits from next-generation process technologies. If returns are inadequate, Intel may be required to write down manufacturing assets and facilities, as occurred in the third quarter of 2024 for the Intel 7 process node.
comparisons.comparison: Similar to AVGO's risk regarding unsuccessful R&D returns, INTC explicitly links innovation expenses and manufacturing investments to the risk of asset write-downs if returns are inadequate. While AVGO warns that unsuccessful returns 'could adversely affect us,' INTC details that inadequate returns from 'next-generation process technologies' may require writing down 'manufacturing assets and facilities,' citing a specific 2024 impairment.

sentences.text: • We make investments in research and development and the slow or unsuccessful return of our investments in research and development could adversely affect us.

We cannot guarantee that we will realize the expected benefits of next-generation process technologies, including the expected cost, performance, power, and density advantages, or that we will achieve an adequate return on our capital and R&D investments, particularly as the development of new nodes has grown increasingly expensive.

In such circumstances, we may be required to write down the value of some of our manufacturing assets and facilities, increasing our expenses, as we were required to do in the third quarter of 2024 with respect to the Intel 7 process node.
